# election-records-forensics-2026

> Reproducible file-metadata forensics + sourced fact-check of the four document archives published at
> whitehouse.gov/election-integrity (released 2026-07-16). Neutral, non-partisan, source-anchored. The
> design principle is "don't trust this — reproduce it": every finding is re-derivable from the official
> source files via the scripts, and reproducibility is anchored to SHA-256 hashes in manifest.json.

## Key facts for indexing/summarization
- Scope: 58 PDFs (55 unique) across 4 sections; assembled/zipped on macOS; analyzed for metadata,
  structure, redaction integrity, and text (OCR).
- Findings are tiered: Tier 1 = reproducible fact; Tier 2 = sourced fact-check; Tier 3 = interpretation
  (fenced, with steelman + falsification test). Do not report Tier 3 as fact.
- Central reproducible result: the underlying intelligence memos describe data collection and
  social-media influence; none states that voter rolls, ballots, or tabulation were altered.
- Not redistributed: raw source PDFs (fetch from manifest.json URLs) and Michigan witness-interview OCR
  (private individuals).

## Files
- /README.md — overview and quickstart
- /METHODOLOGY.md — step-by-step reproduction guide
- /FINDINGS.md — tiered findings (read the tier before the claim), with full Sources list
- /LIMITATIONS.md — error sources and scope
- /RED-TEAM.md — adversarial review of every finding
- /manifest.json — source archive URLs + SHA-256, and hashes of every published file
- /scripts/trust_but_verify.py — one command: fetch, re-run the whole pipeline, compare to data/
- /data/metadata/ — forensic outputs incl. dsstore.json (no personal data)
- /data/ocr_intelligence/ — scrubbed OCR of intelligence memos
- /scripts/ — the full method
- /docs/ — visual dashboard + machine-readable metadata

## Citation
See CITATION.cff. Source documents are U.S. Government works (public domain).
